text:
elaine: Quick sync  running a dry-run before the full retest for the inference auth chain issues. Objective: exercise ephemeral KMS grants, audit export signing, RBAC minimal-scope provisioning, and the evidence validator. Dry-run window: Tue 2025-06-24 09:00 PT.

sam: I'll scope the RBAC. Thinking short-lived service-account creds (OIDC) for this dry-run so we can test token rotation flows, then switch to assume-role for the live run. Thoughts?

mike: OIDC sounds fine for a dry-run. For the KMS path, we'll still use the proxy, but the grant will be limited to Encrypt/Decrypt with key-usage=wraponly. Grant id: dryrun-1745559012.

ops-oncall: I'll pre-create the object prefix s3://redwood-evidence/dryrun/1745559012/ and a manifest placeholder. I'll also generate presigned PUT URLs for the test agents and dump them to the channel DM.

elaine: Evidence items to capture during dry-run:
- audit export from auth-proxy (signed by 'signing-service' using RSA256) -> audit.json.gz + audit.json.gz.sig
- KV-cache manifest -> kv-manifest.json and kv-manifest.json.sha256
- node snapshots -> node-snap.tar.gz + node-snap.sha256
- evidence manifest: evidence.json (includes fallback events and metrics snapshot)

security-bot: Dry-run checklist:
1) RBAC: create role pen-dryrun with ttl=1h (OIDC bound)
2) KMS grant: dryrun-1745559012 created via kms-proxy
3) Signing-service must produce RSA256 signature file next to audit export
4) Manifest notarization: notary-bot will stamp evidence.json -> evidence.json.notary.sig
5) Validator script run to confirm SHA256s
Link: https://intranet.redwood/dryrun-playbook

sam: RBAC proposal (dry-run):
- role: pen-dryrun (OIDC-sub bound)
- permissions: logs:Read, s3:PutObject (restricted prefix), kms:Encrypt/Decrypt (via proxy; wrap-only)
- explicit deny: iam:CreatePolicy, admin:*
I'll open a canary PR and tag @eng-security for review.

mike: KMS proxy flow for this test: OIDC token -> proxy -> limited grant -> wrap/unwrap. We'll log grant usage to /var/log/kms-grants.log and include the log slice in evidence. Grant creation command (ops):
```
/opt/kms-proxy/bin/grant --key-id arn:...:key/abcd --grant-id dryrun-1745559012 --ops wrap,unwrap --ttl 3600
```

ops-oncall: Pre-staging commands I'll run now:
```bash
aws s3api put-object --bucket redwood-evidence --key dryrun/1745559012/manifest-placeholder --body /dev/null
aws s3 presign put s3://redwood-evidence/dryrun/1745559012/ --expires-in 3600 # (pseudo)
/opt/snapshotter/snap --target inference-nodes --out /tmp/node-snap-1745559012.tar.gz
sha256sum /tmp/node-snap-1745559012.tar.gz > /tmp/node-snap-1745559012.sha256
aws s3 cp /tmp/node-snap-1745559012.tar.gz s3://redwood-evidence/dryrun/1745559012/
aws s3 cp /tmp/node-snap-1745559012.sha256 s3://redwood-evidence/dryrun/1745559012/
```
I'll mark these objects with retention=24h and set S3 object lock for the prefix.

elaine: Signing-service should use RSA key with key-id sign-2025-dryrun. Signing API call for auth-proxy will be:
```
POST /internal/signing/sign 
{ "path": "s3://redwood-evidence/dryrun/1745559012/audit.json.gz", "alg": "RS256", "key": "sign-2025-dryrun" }
```
expect audit.json.gz.sig next to the payload.

notary-bot: I will notarize evidence.json after uploads. Notary will append metadata: notarized_by, notarized_at, and produce evidence.json.notary.sig (ed25519).

mike: Add a fallback capture rule for the dry-run: if avg latency > 300ms for 3 consecutive 30s windows or 5xx > 0.5% for 2m, flip traffic to replica variant and log fallback_event.json to the evidence prefix. Include that in evidence.json.

ops-oncall: I'll wire the health-check and produce fallback_event.json when triggered. I'll also stream a view of metrics to the evidence prefix for 2h post-run.

elaine: Post-run validator steps (security runbook):
1) Download artifacts from s3://redwood-evidence/dryrun/1745559012/
2) Verify RSA signature: `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature audit.json.gz.sig audit.json.gz`
3) Verify SHA256s match the provided .sha256 files. Example quick-check: `python -c \"import hashlib,sys;print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read()).hexdigest())\" node-snap-1745559012.tar.gz`
4) Run evidence-validator: `evidence-validator --manifest evidence.json --notary-key notary.pub`
5) If validator passes, attach artifacts to RETEST-222 and mark dry-run PASS.

security-bot: Acceptance for dry-run success: signatures verifiable (RSA + notary), SHA256 checksums match, RBAC teardown executed (no lingering roles), KMS grant usage log present, and evidence-validator returns OK. If any failure, open follow-up ticket RETEST-222-FOLLOWUP.

sam: After dry-run I'll auto-delete role pen-dryrun and rotate signing-service key cache. We'll also run an ephemeral IAM audit: `iam-audit --filter pen-dryrun --since now-24h` and post results.

mike: I'll watch dashboard and bump replication if needed. I'll keep live console open and escalate on-call if fallback flips.

ops-oncall: Pre-signed URLs for uploader sent via DM. I'll post final pre-run verification at T-30m.

elaine: Owners: orchestration=elaine, RBAC=sam, kms-infra=mike, uploads=ops-oncall, notarization=notary-bot, security-verify=security. Please react when youre locked in.

sam: @elaine locked.

mike: :thumbsup: grant created dryrun-1745559012.

ops-oncall: :white_check_mark: s3 prefix and presigned URLs done. T-30m recheck scheduled.

notary-bot: Notary preflight OK  key available notary-2025.

security-bot: Created ticket RETEST-222 and linked s3 prefix. Notifications scheduled 1h/15m before dry-run.

elaine: Great. We'll run and then re-evaluate for the live retest. Thanks everyone.
